newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Moody's lowers Thai banks' debt, deposit ratings. [CORRECTED 18:04 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Moody's lowers Thai banks' debt, deposit ratings. [CORRECTED 18:04 GMT]

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Wednesday it had lowered the senior debt and deposit ratings of five Thai banks to A3 from A2.
The banks were Bangkok Bank, Export-Import Bank of Thailand, Industrial Finance Corporation of Thailand, Siam Commercial Bank, and Thai Farmers' Bank.
Moody's said it made the cuts due to concerns over the asset quality of banks in Thailand and the instability and fragility of the country's entire financial system.
The following rating cuts were made:
Bangkok Bank - the rating of the bank for its long-term deposits and senior debt to A3 from A2.
Export-Import Bank of Thailand - the long-term senior debt rating to A3 from A2.
Industrial Finance Corporation of Thailand - the long-term senior debt rating to A3 from A2.
Siam Commercial Bank - the long-term deposits and senior debt rating to A3 from A2 and the bank financial strength rating to C from C-plus.
Thai Farmers' Bank - the long-term deposits and senior debt to A3 from A2.
Moody's also confirmed the following ratings:
Bangkok Bank - long-term subordinated debt rating of A3, short-term senior obligations rating of Prime-2 and its bank financial strength rating of C.
Siam Commercial Bank - long-term subordinated debt rating of A3 and the short-term senior obligations rating of Prime-2.
Thai Farmers' Bank - long-term subordinated debt rating of A3, short-term senior obligations rating of Prime-2 and the bank financial strength rating of C-plus (Moody's corrects rating).
